about.title: Kerman Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Kerman is a small city, but its roads carry a lot of local and pass-through traffic, especially along Madera Avenue, Whitesbridge Road, California Avenue, and the stretch of Route 180 that runs near town. Public crash records show injury collisions happen here, and Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. see more reported crashes than other times. When you're the one hurt, the aftermath can be confusing: medical visits, missed work, calls from an insurance adjuster who wants a statement. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves. We're a free service that listens to what happened, then connects you with an independent personal injury attorney in our network who can look at your situation and explain your options. There's no cost to you unless the attorney recovers something on your behalf. Our goal is simply to make sure you're not trying to sort through all of this alone right after a crash.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to Someone Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your Kerman crash before it passes.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Your compensation is simply reduced by your percentage of fault, so it's worth having someone evaluate the full picture rather than assuming a partial fault means no case.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Wait
items.desc: Insurance companies often ask for a recorded statement quickly, before you've seen a doctor or reviewed the evidence. You're not required to give one right away, and speaking with an attorney first can help protect your claim and preserve details like skid marks, damage, or witness accounts before they're lost.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Kerman?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned vehicle or a road maintained by a public entity, that deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months. It's best to have an attorney confirm your specific timeline as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the crash happened on Whitesbridge Road or Route 180 and I wasn't sure who was at fault?
items.answer: California's pure comparative fault rule means you can still pursue compensation even if you share some blame for the accident. An attorney can review the police report, any available evidence, and witness statements from the scene to help sort out how fault should be divided. Being unsure of fault at the scene doesn't mean you don't have a claim.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company before hiring an attorney?
items.answer: It's generally a good idea to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other insurer until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters sometimes ask questions designed to minimize your claim before you've had a chance to fully understand your injuries or the accident details. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can advise you on what, if anything, to say.
